## AI-Powered IB Coursework Grading Services


AI-powered IB coursework grading services assess drafts against assessment criteria and return feedback before submission. They can identify missing analysis, weak evidence, unclear structure, citation problems, and sections that do not demonstrate the required skills. However, an AI report is a revision tool, not an official IB mark or a replacement for your teacher’s guidance.


The important question is not whether an AI grader can produce a number. It is whether the tool connects comments to the correct IB rubric, explains its judgement, and gives you actions for your next draft. RevisionDojo’s Coursework Grader is designed for IB Internal Assessments, Extended Essays, and Theory of Knowledge essays, with rubric-based annotations and criterion-level feedback.


This article explains how AI grading works, how reliable it can be, where human judgement remains necessary, and how to use a coursework grading service responsibly.


### Accuracy and Reliability of AI Grading


### How AI graders evaluate IB coursework


An AI coursework grader typically identifies the coursework type, subject, level, research question or prescribed title, argument, evidence, structure, and academic conventions. It then compares those features with relevant assessment criteria and markband descriptors.


This differs from asking a general chatbot whether an essay is good. A rubric-based system should ask more specific questions: Does the essay answer the research question? Is evidence analysed rather than merely described? Is the argument sustained? Does the conclusion follow from the investigation? Are required reflections or methodological decisions demonstrated where relevant?


The quality of feedback depends heavily on selecting the correct rubric. A Biology IA, History IA, subject-specific EE, and TOK essay do not reward exactly the same forms of evidence or reasoning. RevisionDojo’s Coursework Grader asks students to choose the coursework type, subject, and level where applicable before generating feedback. Students can[open the IB Coursework Grader](https://www.revisiondojo.com/grader) to review the available options.


### What rubric alignment means


The IB uses criterion-related assessment. Work is judged against stated expectations rather than simply ranked against other students’ submissions. The official Extended Essay guidance identifies criteria including **focus and method** , **knowledge and understanding** , **critical thinking** , **presentation** , and **engagement** . Interpretation also depends on subject-specific guidance.


A useful AI report should separate feedback by criterion instead of giving one unexplained percentage. An EE report might recognise a focused research question but explain that the analysis does not yet support a sustained conclusion. An IA report might recognise appropriate data collection while noting that evaluation of limitations is too general. A TOK report might distinguish between relevant examples and examples that are not sufficiently connected to the knowledge question.


RevisionDojo describes its Coursework Grader as evaluating **IA, EE, and TOK essays** . Reports can include inline annotations, a criterion-by-criterion breakdown, an overall summary, and targeted next steps. Students can also use the[IB IA Guides](https://www.revisiondojo.com/ia-guides) ,[IB Extended Essay Guide](https://www.revisiondojo.com/ee-guides) , and[IB coursework exemplars](https://www.revisiondojo.com/coursework-exemplars) to compare feedback with guidance and examples.


### Can an AI grader be accurate?


AI grading can be useful when it consistently identifies rubric-relevant features and explains its reasoning. It is particularly effective for checking visible qualities such as organisation, repeated description, missing sections, unsupported claims, word-count issues, unclear transitions, and whether paragraphs address the stated question.


It is less dependable when judgement depends on subtle context. A human assessor may understand why an unusual method was appropriate, recognise a sophisticated but unconventional argument, or interpret the significance of research decisions from reflections. An AI system may also misunderstand a diagram, formula, source, quotation, or disciplinary convention if the document is poorly formatted or the selected rubric is wrong.


An AI-generated mark should therefore be treated as an estimate for drafting, not a prediction of the final result. The most reliable use is to look for patterns across drafts. If the same criterion repeatedly receives feedback about insufficient evaluation, that pattern deserves investigation. If a comment conflicts with your subject guide or teacher’s explanation, verify it rather than changing your work automatically.


The IB’s own guidance should remain the reference point. Consult the[official Extended Essay subject-specific guidance](https://ibpublishing.ibo.org/extendedessay/apps/dpapp/guidance.html?doc=d_0_eeyyy_gui_1602_1_e) and the[IB Theory of Knowledge programme information](https://www.ibo.org/globalassets/new-structure/programmes/dp/pdfs/tok-sb-english.pdf) . These documents clarify the formal expectations an AI tool is attempting to interpret.


### AI grading compared with teacher feedback


AI and teacher feedback serve different purposes. An AI grader can review a draft quickly, apply the same checklist repeatedly, and point directly to passages needing attention. A teacher or supervisor can interpret your progress, ask questions about your decisions, identify misunderstandings, and advise you within the context of your course and school.


The distinction is especially important for the EE. Engagement relates to the research and writing process, including how you reflect on decisions and respond to challenges. An AI can comment on written reflections, but it cannot independently verify what happened during your research. Similarly, it can flag a weak TOK example but cannot replace the judgement involved in deciding which real-life situation genuinely advances your argument.


Use AI feedback as a first or second review before discussing the draft with your teacher. Bring specific questions, such as why a paragraph appears descriptive under the analysis criterion or which evidence would make a limitation more precise. This turns automated comments into a productive academic conversation.


### Detailed Feedback and Professional Standards


### Why criterion-level feedback matters


A general comment such as “add more detail” is difficult to act on. Criterion-level feedback connects the problem to an assessment objective and identifies the type of revision required.


For example, a student might receive this sequence:


1. The research question is focused, but the introduction does not explain why the method can answer it.
2. The body includes relevant sources, but paragraphs summarise them separately instead of comparing their implications.
3. The conclusion repeats findings but does not evaluate the limits of the evidence.
4. The next draft should connect each major claim to evidence and explain how that evidence changes the answer to the research question.


This is more practical than a single projected grade because it tells you what to change. It also helps you prioritise: students often correct wording while leaving major weaknesses in analysis or evaluation unresolved.

Reported outputs include:

The service is intended for iterative drafting. You can review an early version, revise weak sections, and check the updated draft again. This creates a feedback loop: draft, inspect the criterion, revise the evidence or reasoning, and check whether the change solved the original problem.


### How to use an AI grader effectively


Start with a clean document and choose the correct coursework type, subject, and level. Include the sections you want assessed, along with relevant figures, tables, and appendices where the platform permits them. A poorly scanned PDF, missing graph, or incorrect rubric can produce feedback that is less useful than the document deserves.


Read the report in three passes:


- **First pass: overall diagnosis.** Identify the two or three issues affecting the largest number of criteria.
- **Second pass: annotations.** Locate the exact sentences, paragraphs, calculations, or examples connected to each comment.
- **Third pass: revision plan.** Convert feedback into actions, such as comparing sources, explaining a limitation, refining a claim, or linking an example to the research question.


Do not ask the tool to write the complete IA, EE, or TOK essay. That can weaken your understanding and create academic-integrity concerns. Your reasoning, evidence selection, reflection, and final writing must remain central to the submission.


For TOK, ask whether each example is doing analytical work rather than simply illustrating a point. For an IA, check whether method, data processing, analysis, and evaluation answer the investigation question. For an EE, examine whether the research question, source use, argument, conclusion, and reflections form a coherent process.


### Professional standards and responsible use


Professional-quality feedback is not defined by a confident tone or high predicted mark. It requires traceable reasoning, appropriate rubric use, clear limitations, and actionable recommendations. A report should explain why a section is weak and what evidence or analysis would strengthen it.


Protect your academic integrity and personal data. Follow your school’s rules about AI assistance, keep records of your own drafting and research process, and do not present generated language or analysis as your own work. Use plagiarism or AI-checking software only as an additional review, not as proof that a document is acceptable.


A practical workflow is to draft independently, run the Coursework Grader, verify disputed points against official criteria, discuss important issues with your supervisor, and rewrite in your own words.
